bigpic.b: Megadeals swept tech, pharma and telecoms
bigpic.t: as CrowdStrike agreed a $43.9B Zscaler takeover, Sanofi a $41B Insmed buyout, and StarHub and M1 an all-share merger.

bigpic.b: Asia's chip rally met a cooler Wall Street
bigpic.t: as the Kospi closed above 5,000 but US futures slipped and Nvidia fell about 4% premarket after Monday's 31% jump.

bigpic.b: US chip curbs reached deeper into Southeast Asia
bigpic.t: as an Alibaba unit joined Megaspeed firms on a blacklist; Singapore's prime minister says investigations are continuing.

stories.h: Kospi closes above 5,000, but US futures slip as Nvidia gives back 4% premarket
stories.sum: South Korea's Kospi closed 6.32% higher at 5,006.04 and the Nikkei 3.91% at 58,644.63 on Tuesday, led by Kioxia, SK Hynix and Samsung. Wall Street futures then turned lower: at 4:30am ET Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.61%, with Nvidia about 4% lower and HPE down 9.6% after big Monday gains.
stories.why: Investors are testing whether Monday's AI relief rally can hold with a Fed hike and hot inflation data still ahead.

stories.h: S&P 500 exits correction with its biggest gain in over 18 months
stories.sum: The S&P 500 rose 4.74% to 7,237.90 on Monday, ending a seven-session losing streak and leaving correction territory. The Nasdaq gained 6.51% and the Dow 3.01%, or 1,448 points, while the VIX fell about 26% to 26.6. Gainers beat decliners roughly five to one on the NYSE.
stories.why: The rebound eases fears of a wider unwind, but inflation data and the 9 Dec Fed decision still hang over valuations.

stories.h: Holiday week: PCE inflation on Wednesday, markets shut Thursday
stories.sum: October PCE inflation, the second Q3 GDP estimate and durable goods orders all land Wednesday, with jobless claims brought forward a day. Economists expect headline PCE of 3.6% and core of 3.2%. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shut at 1pm ET on Friday.
stories.why: Thin holiday trading can exaggerate moves after one of the most volatile stretches of the year.

stories.h: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9B in an all-stock cybersecurity megadeal
stories.sum: Zscaler holders will get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, about $260.41 a share and a 34% premium to the 20 Nov close, leaving CrowdStrike owners with 84.1%. Founder Jay Chaudhry will keep running Zscaler. The firms target $1B in yearly revenue synergies, with closing in the second half of fiscal 2028. CrowdStrike fell 8.92% on Monday.
stories.why: Folds network and zero-trust security into CrowdStrike's platform, a big step in the industry's consolidation into a few all-in-one suppliers.

stories.h: Nvidia slips premarket after its 31% surge on Huang's return as CEO
stories.sum: Shares closed up 31.48% at $165.05 on Monday after the board reinstated Jensen Huang, less than two weeks after he resigned, but were down about 4% before Tuesday's open. The board is still investigating whether Huang was targeted by a foreign spy, and he is due to testify to the Senate Banking Committee on 3 Dec.
stories.why: Restores the AI chip leader's founder, but a foreign-intelligence probe and export-control scrutiny remain open.

stories.h: Alibaba unit among seven Southeast Asian firms on new US chip blacklist
stories.sum: Commerce's rule adds Megaspeed entities and partners in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, including Alibaba's Apex Enterprise Solutions, which prepaid about $4.2B for computing capacity. Exports to them need licences that face a presumption of denial. Alibaba called the listing erroneous and plans legal action; Singapore PM Lawrence Wong said investigations continue.
stories.why: Puts Singapore and Malaysia's data-centre hubs under sharper scrutiny as Washington targets AI chip diversion to China.

stories.h: Xiaomi's third-quarter adjusted profit falls 57% and misses forecasts
stories.sum: Adjusted net profit fell 56.8% to 4.88B yuan, below the 5.2B yuan analysts expected, while revenue slipped 5.2% to 107.24B yuan, ahead of estimates. Smartphones and AIoT brought in 83.35B yuan and the EV, AI and new initiatives unit 23.88B yuan. Xiaomi has spent about HK$13.1B on buybacks this year.
stories.why: Shows the squeeze on China's consumer-tech giants as phone demand cools while EV and AI spending stays heavy.

stories.h: Treasury yields lower after inflation warning from New York Fed's Williams, investors await 5-year auction
Fed hike all but priced in as Williams warns inflation is too high
stories.sum: Traders price about a 95% chance of a quarter-point increase on 9 Dec and 5% for a half-point move. New York Fed President John Williams said on 23 Nov he would not rule out back-to-back hikes and sees inflation reaching 2% only in 2028. October PCE data lands Wednesday, with core expected at 3.2%.
stories.why: Higher policy rates lift banks' funding and deposit costs and raise credit risk for stretched borrowers.

stories.h: JPMorgan and HSBC complete first trades in tokenised London gold
stories.sum: JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX traded digital ownership of portions of vaulted gold bars in London last week under the World Gold Council's Pooled Gold Interests structure, and tested the holdings as collateral, Bloomberg reported. Trade sizes were not disclosed and the system is still in trial.
stories.why: Fractional, tokenised gold could make bullion easier to use as collateral and widen banks' gold financing business.

stories.h: Straits Energy Disputes RM10 Million Payment Default Claims
South Korea's crypto bill lifts the ICO ban and gives banks control of won stablecoins
stories.sum: The FSC's draft ends a ban on coin offerings in place since 2017, if issuers publish white papers. Won stablecoins must come from consortia more than 50% owned by banks, with full reserves and no interest paid. Major exchange shareholders face a 20% cap, or 34% with approval. The bill could reach parliament by 25 Nov.
stories.why: Sets how Korea's large retail crypto market will be run, and hands banks rather than fintechs the lead on stablecoins.

stories.h: CFTC lets US exchanges count bitcoin, ether and stablecoins toward reserves
stories.sum: A staff advisory on 23 Nov says swap facilities, futures exchanges and clearing houses can count bitcoin, ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward the resources covering 12 months of operating costs, after haircuts of at least 20% for the coins and 2% for stablecoins. They still cannot count toward liquidity requirements.
stories.why: Another step in bringing crypto onto the balance sheets of regulated US market infrastructure.

stories.h: Bitcoin hovers near $60,000 as ETF outflows top $4B this month
stories.sum: Bitcoin was down about 2.3% near $60,000 on Tuesday, after briefly touching $64,500 on Huang's return to Nvidia. US spot bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $4B in November, and the Crypto Fear & Greed Index sits at 11, signalling extreme fear.
stories.why: Crypto is lagging the stock rebound, a sign that ETF and leveraged money has not come back.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price. It gains Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Insmed rose about 14% early and Sanofi about 5% in Paris.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: Health insurers slide as Medicare proposes a tougher star-ratings system
stories.sum: UnitedHealth fell 6.5%, Humana 5.1% and CVS 4.5% before Monday's open after CMS proposed overhauling Medicare Advantage star ratings, which set bonus payments. TD Cowen, citing CMS estimates, said the change would cut payments by about $107B over 2028 to 2037. It is a proposal, not a final rule.
stories.why: Star-rating bonuses are a key source of Medicare Advantage profit, so cuts would squeeze insurers' margins from 2031.

stories.h: FDA approves AbbVie's Rinvoq as first systemic vitiligo treatment
stories.sum: The once-daily 15mg pill is cleared for adults and children 12 and older with nonsegmental vitiligo. In two Phase 3 trials, 25% and 23% of patients reached at least 75% facial repigmentation at week 48, against 6% and 7% on placebo.
stories.why: Gives dermatologists a first pill option for a common skin disease with few effective treatments.

stories.h: Oil shrugs off Iran's claim that three tankers hit mines in Hormuz
stories.sum: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said three tankers that broke its new crossing rules struck mines and caught fire; the claim has not been verified and traders largely dismissed it. Brent was at $89.10, down 0.3%, at 07:00 GMT after touching its lowest since 27 Aug, with WTI at $79.97.
stories.why: A supply surplus is outweighing Gulf risk for now, but Tehran's talk of escorted convoys to break the US blockade keeps a shock possible.

stories.h: South Korea asks Qatar for priority LNG once Hormuz shipping returns to normal
stories.sum: Trade and energy minister Kim Jung-kwan made the request to Qatar's energy minister Saad al-Kaabi in Seoul on 23 Nov. QatarEnergy has extended its LNG force majeure month by month since April, most recently to the end of December, and South Korea has leaned on coal to fill the gap.
stories.why: Shows Asian importers jostling for scarce Gulf LNG, which keeps winter gas supply tight for import-dependent economies.

stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday to set 2027 output baselines
stories.sum: The 29 Nov ministerial meeting is expected to agree a 2027 framework based on a capacity review, since group-wide targets run only to 31 Dec. Seven core members have held combined output targets at 31.01M barrels a day.
stories.why: New baselines decide who can pump more next year as the market tips toward surplus.

stories.h: Tesla and SpaceX name five directors to steer possible merger talks, FT reports
stories.sum: Tesla directors Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung and SpaceX's Roelof Botha and Randy Glein will guide special committees weighing an all-stock combination, the FT reported on 24 Nov. Evercore advises Tesla, and Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs advise SpaceX. Neither company commented; Bloomberg has said a deal could come as soon as December.
stories.why: A merger would tie Tesla's car business to Musk's rocket and satellite empire, changing how investors value the EV maker.

stories.h: Waymo pulls its robotaxis off US freeways and files two safety recalls
stories.sum: Waymo paused freeway driving in all its markets after California's DMV banned it over robotaxis entering construction zones, and filed NHTSA recalls covering closed freeway lanes and police-directed intersections. NHTSA has also opened a recall query into nearly 3,000 Waymo vehicles over passing school buses.
stories.why: Regulators are pushing back as robotaxi fleets move onto faster roads, which could slow commercial rollouts across the industry.

stories.h: Electric cars take 31% of Europe's market as Skoda Elroq outsells Tesla Model Y
stories.sum: Battery-electric registrations in the EU, UK and EFTA rose 57% to 346,708 in October, a 31% share against 21% a year earlier, according to preliminary Dataforce figures. Skoda's Elroq was the top EV with 9,384 sales, ahead of the Model Y on 8,309.
stories.why: European buyers are switching to EVs faster, and legacy brands are taking share from Tesla.

stories.h: Best Buy, Dick's and Abercrombie test shoppers before Black Friday
stories.sum: Best Buy, Dick's Sporting Goods, Abercrombie & Fitch and Kohl's report on Tuesday, with Urban Outfitters after the close. Bets against the group are heavy: short interest is 30.1% of Kohl's float and 17.4% for Dick's.
stories.why: These are the last big reads on consumer health before the holiday weekend.

stories.h: Fewer Americans expected to shop over Thanksgiving weekend
stories.sum: The NRF and Prosper Insights expect 182.7 million shoppers over the holiday weekend, down more than 2%, as 60% had started buying by early November. About 82% say they are looking for ways to limit holiday spending.
stories.why: Earlier, more cautious shopping blunts the Black Friday spike that retailers rely on.

stories.h: US holiday sales forecast to top $1 trillion for the first time
stories.sum: The NRF expects November–December retail sales of $1.013T, up 4.2%. Bain sees Black Friday through Cyber Monday above $85B. Visa's 4.5% growth forecast works out to about 1.1% after inflation.
stories.why: Most headline growth is higher prices; real volume growth is thin.

stories.h: Disney's Hexed and Universal's Focker In-Law open into a key Thanksgiving test
stories.sum: Both films open on Wednesday. Deadline's early forecasts put each at $40M to $50M over five days, though Box Office Theory has cut Hexed to about $23M. The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping, which opened to an estimated $120M, could top both in its second weekend.
stories.why: Thanksgiving is a major test for cinemas after the five-day haul fell to $290.3M in 2025 from $424.9M in 2024.

stories.h: Disney hits a 52-week high while Netflix is down 36% this year
stories.sum: Disney has been lifted by parks, cruises and a 97% jump in streaming operating income. Netflix has fallen 36.2% in 2026 after cutting its ad revenue forecast by $300M and raising prices three times in under three years.
stories.why: Investors are favouring diversified media groups over pure-play streamers as subscription growth slows.

stories.h: Dozens of CBS News staff take Skydance buyouts
stories.sum: Producers, editors and operations staff from Evening News, 60 Minutes and CBS Mornings accepted buyouts from parent Skydance, with the London bureau hit hardest. No exact headcount was given.
stories.why: Post-merger cost cutting is now reaching news divisions as owners chase savings.

stories.h: FAA braces for its busiest Thanksgiving in 16 years, with 417,775 flights planned
stories.sum: The FAA expects 417,775 flights over the nine days to 1 Dec, up 2.2% on last year and 7.5% on 2019, with Tuesday the peak at more than 52,000. The TSA expects nearly 17.6 million passengers from Tuesday to Monday, and airlines nearly 29 million over 20 to 30 Nov.
stories.why: A smooth holiday would ease pressure on the air traffic system after the 13 Nov ground stop disrupted more than 18,000 flights.

stories.h: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial jet workforce as the 737 MAX ramp slips
stories.sum: Boeing Commercial Airplanes, with about 50,000 staff, plans the cuts through attrition and layoffs, with notices expected around 9 Dec. Its goal of building 47 MAX jets a month has slipped to early 2027, and October deliveries fell to 49 from 57 in September, including 32 MAXs.
stories.why: Slower MAX output delays jets airlines need for growth and squeezes suppliers who planned for higher rates.

stories.h: Airbus workers push for a German-led fighter after the FCAS jet project stalls
stories.sum: With the FCAS fighter stalled by disputes between Airbus and Dassault, Airbus staff at Manching backed a national sixth-generation jet on 23 Nov, aiming for a first flight in 2032. Airbus has formed an industry group, Team Gen 6, though it has no government funding. Defence Minister Boris Pistorius expects a decision in early 2027.
stories.why: The outcome will shape Europe's next combat-jet partnerships and decide billions in defence work for Airbus, Dassault and suppliers.

stories.h: US housing braces for a harsh winter as sales slump
stories.sum: Pending home sales were down nearly 17% from a year earlier in October, and MBA purchase applications ran 18% below last year in mid-November. Real REMAX expects 2027 existing-home sales to fall 5% to 10% and national prices 3% to 4%.
stories.why: With 30-year mortgage rates near 7.1% and a Fed hike coming, a quick recovery looks unlikely.

stories.h: China's home prices seen falling again in 2027, Reuters poll shows
stories.sum: Analysts expect prices to fall 2.8% this year and 0.5% in 2027, a deeper 2027 drop than the 0.3% seen in August. Property investment is forecast to slump 22% in 2026 and sales 14%, both worse than in the previous poll.
stories.why: A longer slump keeps pressure on Chinese developers, local-government finances and demand for building materials.

stories.h: Blue Owl buys a 54MW northern Virginia data center for $779.5M
stories.sum: Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust, a non-traded REIT affiliated with Blue Owl Capital, paid $779.5M for a 54-megawatt data center on the Gainesville Crossing campus in Gainesville, Virginia. The sellers are affiliates of Affinius Capital.
stories.why: Private real estate money keeps flowing into data centers, the strongest corner of commercial property in the AI boom.

stories.h: StarHub and M1 agree an all-share merger creating a S$5B Singapore telco
stories.sum: StarHub will issue about 651.7 million new shares, 27.4% of the enlarged group, to M1's owners, giving the combination an enterprise value of S$5B (US$3.87B). Keppel, which owns about 84% of M1, will hold 23%. The firms target S$110M of yearly cost savings by 2030; completion is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to IMDA approval.
stories.why: Consolidation in Singapore's crowded mobile market could ease price competition and lift returns for the remaining operators.

stories.h: KLCI snaps a five-day losing streak as chip stocks lead; ringgit firms
stories.sum: The FBM KLCI closed up 12.63 points, or 0.81%, at 1,561.68, with gainers beating losers 751 to 360. Malaysian Pacific Industries rose RM1.80 and ViTrox 45 sen, while Maybank added 25 sen. The ringgit strengthened to 4.1135 per US dollar at 6pm from 4.1205 on Monday.
stories.why: Malaysia's chip and data-centre stocks track the AI cycle, though analysts expect caution ahead of US inflation data.

stories.h: Singapore lifts 2026 growth forecast to about 6% after Q3 GDP jumps 6.1%
stories.sum: Third-quarter growth was revised up to 6.1% year on year from a 5.4% advance estimate, beating forecasts of 5.6%, led by AI-driven electronics output and wholesale trade. The trade ministry raised its 2026 forecast from 4.5% to 5.5% to around 6%, and expects 2.5% to 4.5% growth in 2027.
stories.why: Confirms AI exports are powering Singapore, though officials warn a turn in the AI cycle could hit markets hard.
